sentences.text:
ORAL JUDGMENT . Heard.
2.
By this appeal, the challenge is to the order passed by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gadchiroli of granting compensation to the claimant under Section 140 of the Motor Vehicle Act.
3. The perusal of the record shows that the deceased was travelling in Matador bearing No.MH-35/1796 towards Korchi on 03.06.2009.
At that time, one unknown truck coming from the opposite side gave dash to the Matador and Matador turned turtle.
In the said accident, the deceased succumbed to the injuries.
4. The legal heirs, therefore, filed a Claim Petition before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal.
Along with the claim petition, they have moved the application for interim compensation under Section 140 of the Motor Vehicle Act.
Accordingly, the learned Tribunal awarded Rs.50,000/- to the applicants and directed to be deposited within a stipulated time period.
5. This Court vide order dated 11.07.2012 admitted the matter and called the record and proceedings.
As a result, the present appeal is pending on the file of this Court since year 2012.

6. It is seen from the record that the respondents are duly served in the matter and they have engaged the advocate in the matter, but no one appeared today when the matter is taken for final disposal.

7. It is well settled position of law that under Section 140 of the Motor Vehicle Act where death of any person has caused due to an accident arising out of the use of the motor vehicle, the owner of the vehicle or the Insurance Company are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation in respect of such death in accordance with the provisions of law.
This arrangement is made by the statute to provide the monetary help to the family of the deceased who is facing financial crises due to untimely death of the bread earner of the family.

8. However appellant herein made exception to the order passed by the learned Tribunal by raising a ground that the Matador being a goods vehicle was not supposed to carry the passengers and,
therefore, it is a breach of terms of policy and, therefore, the appellant- Insurance Company is not responsible to pay the compensation amount.
9. As already stated, the respondents are served, but no one appeared in the matter and ground which is raised by appellant cannot be decided at this stage of the matter.

Only after full trial,
appropriate conclusion can be drawn in the matter.

sentences.text: It is pointed out that due to non availability of record and proceeding before the Claim Tribunal Gadchiroli, the matter has not been proceeded further and same is still pending on the file of Claim Tribunal, Gadchiroli.

11. In the circumstances, I am of the opinion that instead of deciding the present appeal on its own merit, the amount which is deposited by the appellant before this Court can be transferred to the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gadchiroli and the Tribunal can be directed to decide the pending petition expeditiously and the amount towards 'No Fault Liability' will be allowed to be withdrawn subject to the final decision of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal.

Hence, I proceed to pass the following order in the matter:
ORDER i) The First Appeal is partly allowed.
ii) The amount deposited by the appellant towards 'No Fault Liability' i.e.
Rs.50,000/- along with interest accrued thereon be transferred to the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gadchiroli.
iii) The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gadchiroli is directed to decide the Claim Petition No.34/2011 as expeditiously as possible on its own merits.
iv) The amount transferred to the Claim Tribunal shall be disbursed in terms of the final judgment of the Tribunal.
12. The appeal stands disposed of accordingly.
(PRAVIN S. PATIL, J.) R.S. Sahare Signed by: Mrs. Ranjana Sahare Designation: PA To Honourable Judge Date: 06/11/2025 18:06:36
